candidateDecisions.label: Movement, Health and Behavior
candidateDecisions.assessment: Medical and health psychology, lifespan development, physiology, epidemiology and qualitative methods support study of activity and recovery in social context. The plan is focused on health behavior. Dedicated sport psychology and rehabilitation practice require further study.

candidateDecisions.label: Sports performance and talent development
candidateDecisions.assessment: General human physiology introduces exercise and metabolism, while linear systems and computer vision offer measurement tools. There is insufficient cumulative coursework in exercise testing, training adaptation, sport performance and talent development for a dedicated UCR plan.

analysis: Both plans develop body systems, neural control and perception and use statistics and research synthesis. The measurement plan advances from programming, mathematical methods and linear algebra to numerical methods, linear systems, probability, machine learning and computer vision. Feature tracking and signal processing are relevant tools for motion analysis, while specialist force, gait and exercise testing require different equipment and progression. The health and behavior plan develops psychopathology, psychological assessment, health psychology and lifespan development around activity and coping. Biochemistry supports metabolism. Sociology and qualitative methods add attention to social barriers and lived experience using interviews and thematic analysis. Philosophy of Mind contributes a conceptual account of the mind–body relation. The plan studies recovery-related questions within broader health psychology and makes no claim to therapist training or a dedicated sport-psychology sequence. The original second plan placed Image Processing in an unavailable term, and the same course set is infeasible even after rescheduling with the academic sequence constraints. Retaining vision in the measurement plan and refocusing three selections in the second plan gives each a defensible sequence. The eight shared rows describe focused overlap. Dedicated movement pathology, lab analysis, exercise testing, sport psychology and the compulsory project are shown separately. Lifespan development includes psychomotor development, but does not constitute a specialist motor learning course. A sport-performance and talent plan lacks cumulative exercise measurement and performance-specific training in the active workbook.
